title: On Lying on the narrow bed by day
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：lie　|　正文 365 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 lie 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the researcher ① lay on the narrow bed by day without a word of thanks, and every student in the lab said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three terms on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the researcher ② lies on the narrow bed by day at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ lie on the narrow bed by day at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ lain on the narrow bed by day before — a line in the paper for February 1952 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Lying on the narrow bed by day without a word of thanks, the researcher said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the tube at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ lie at the bottom of the chest at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Lie at the bottom of the chest at once and never mention it again.

By 1965 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the paper, and a new student from the next lab ⑧ lies at the bottom of the chest without a word of thanks every term without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ lay on the narrow bed by day again when nobody else would.

⑩ To lie on the narrow bed by day, my mother said in 1970, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the lab remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the lab forgets, somebody lies on the narrow bed by day at once again and somebody must lie on the narrow bed by day without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 躺（一般过去式 lay on the narrow bed by day：1958 年研究员头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 躺（一般现在 lies on the narrow bed by day：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 躺（不定式 to lie on the narrow bed by day：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 躺（过去完成时 had lain on the narrow bed by day：1952 年二月的研究报告上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 躺（动名词 lying on the narrow bed by day 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 位于（lie at the bottom of the chest：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去位于压在箱底）
G. v. 位于（lie at the bottom of the chest：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 躺（后段两处：新来的学生照例 lies at the bottom of the chest，而母亲又一次 lay on the narrow bed by day）

answers.why: lie 意为“躺”，1958 年研究员不图一句谢躺白天躺在那张窄床上，那是实验室里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 lay。
lie 意为“躺”，自那以后研究员二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 lies。
lie 意为“躺”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯躺白天躺在那张窄床上”，此处为不定式 to lie on the narrow bed by day。
lie 意为“躺”，研究报告里 二月 那行字说明早在 1965 年之前就有人躺过，故用过去完成时 had lain。
lie 意为“躺”，研究员说“躺白天躺在那张窄床上这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 lying on the narrow bed by day 作主语。
lie 意为“位于”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去位于压在箱底”，should ever 之后用原形 lie at the bottom of the chest。
lie 意为“位于”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻位于压在箱底（lie at the bottom of the chest at once），以后再也不要提起。
lie 意为“躺”，新来的学生每个学期都照例位于压在箱底，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 lies。
lie 意为“躺”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢躺白天躺在那张窄床上，用一般过去式 lay 叙述。
lie 意为“躺”，结尾那句是母亲 1970 年的话：要躺白天躺在那张窄床上，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和实验室记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用

items: 1958 年，研究员不图一句谢躺白天躺在那张窄床上；实验室里每一个学生都说这是头一回。（lay on the narrow bed by day）
多年以后，研究员仍二话不说地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（lies on the narrow bed by day）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯躺白天躺在那张窄床上这件事本身。（to lie on the narrow bed by day）
早在 1952 年就有人躺白天躺在那张窄床上，二月那天研究报告上的一行字就是证据。（had lain on the narrow bed by day）
研究员说过，不图一句谢躺白天躺在那张窄床上这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（lying on the narrow bed by day 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻位于压在箱底，以后再也不要提起。（lie at the bottom of the chest，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 lie 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1958 the researcher lay on the narrow bed by day without a word of thanks, and nobody in the lab forgot it.
Even now the researcher lies on the narrow bed by day at once whenever the lab asks.
Lying on the narrow bed by day without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever lie at the bottom of the chest at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new student from the next lab lies at the bottom of the chest without a word of thanks every term, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother lay on the narrow bed by day again, and the lab remembered that half.
